XMLDB.COMMENT: Interactive video, forked from H5P Interactive Video. The interaction shape follows the upstream semantics.json closely enough that content is convertible; the correct answers are the one part that does not follow it, because here they never leave the server.

FIELD.NAME: videourl
FIELD.COMMENT: Empty when the video is an uploaded file. The file area is the truth and this is the fallback, exactly as in mod_kaivideo.

FIELD.NAME: posterstart
FIELD.COMMENT: Show the start screen with the title before playing.

FIELD.NAME: showendscreen
FIELD.COMMENT: The forked endscreen, showing the learner their own submitted score. Rendered from what the server sent back, never from anything the browser worked out.

FIELD.NAME: mustanswer
FIELD.COMMENT: Playback refuses to continue past an unanswered required interaction. Enforced by the due rule (playhead at or past the point and unanswered) rather than by watching for a skip, so dragging the seekbar is the same case as playing.

FIELD.NAME: maxattempts
FIELD.COMMENT: Attempts per interaction, 0 meaning unlimited. While attempts remain and the last one was wrong, the server withholds both the correct answer and the feedback: releasing the explanation early turns retry into a button that hands out marks.

TABLE.NAME: kaiiv_interaction
TABLE.COMMENT: One thing placed on the timeline. The presentation columns mirror what the forked player expects; the content columns are ours.

FIELD.NAME: endtime
FIELD.COMMENT: When the interaction stops being on screen. Equal to starttime for the kinds that pause the video, because those end when they are answered and not when a clock runs out.

FIELD.NAME: type
FIELD.COMMENT: choice, multichoice, truefalse, shorttext, blanks, dragtext, marktheword, label, image or link. Which of those are graded is declared in classes/interaction_type.php; that list and this column must not drift.

FIELD.NAME: displaytype
FIELD.COMMENT: poster (drawn onto the video) or button (a marker the learner opens). Graded interactions that pause the video are forced to poster on save: a question the learner can decline to open is not a question the video can refuse to continue past.

FIELD.NAME: x
FIELD.COMMENT: Percent of the video width. Percentages rather than pixels because the same activity is watched on a phone and on a projector.

FIELD.NAME: label
FIELD.COMMENT: Shown on the marker and read out by screen readers. Not the question text: a marker that gives the question away before it is opened defeats the point of a button interaction.

FIELD.NAME: content
FIELD.COMMENT: JSON of everything the browser is allowed to see: question text, options, sentences with the gaps blanked out, image ids, link targets.

FIELD.NAME: answers
FIELD.COMMENT: JSON of the correct answer. Never in any payload sent to a browser that is taking the activity. This column is the reason the fork does not use H5P.Question.

FIELD.NAME: sortorder
FIELD.COMMENT: Tie-break for two interactions at the same second, so the order an author set is the order shown.

TABLE.NAME: kaiiv_bookmark
TABLE.COMMENT: A named point on the timeline. No grading and no state; it exists so a learner can find a section again.

TABLE.NAME: kaiiv_response
TABLE.COMMENT: What one learner answered, every time they answered it.

FIELD.NAME: response
FIELD.COMMENT: Kept verbatim, so a teacher sees what was said and not only whether it was accepted.

FIELD.NAME: category
FIELD.COMMENT: The category as it stood when this was answered, copied rather than read back through the interaction: recategorising a question next term must not rewrite what last term said about a cohort.

TABLE.NAME: kaiiv_progress
TABLE.COMMENT: How far one learner has got. Every attempt is in kaiiv_response; this is the summary the activity reads.

FIELD.NAME: furthest
FIELD.COMMENT: Furthest point reached. Never rewound by watching again, which is also what makes it safe to send twice from pagehide and visibilitychange.
